learningObjective: Define what a FakeTensor is in PyTorch 2 and describe its role during tracing.

canonicalClaims.claim: A FakeTensor is a tensor-like object carrying shape/dtype/device/stride metadata without a real data buffer; the tracer uses each ATen op's meta implementation to propagate FakeTensors through the traced graph, obtaining output metadata without executing real kernels.
conditions: The traced ops all have meta implementations.
nonImplications: Does not imply FakeTensor tracing captures data-dependent behavior.
Does not imply every op can propagate as a FakeTensor; some ops need real data and cause specialization or graph breaks.

misconceptions.claim: FakeTensors carry real data on GPU.
misconceptions.whyWrong: They have no data buffer; only metadata.

misconceptions.claim: FakeTensors are a TorchScript concept unrelated to torch.compile.
misconceptions.whyWrong: They are central to torch.compile's tracing model.

misconceptions.claim: TorchDynamo uses FakeTensors to numerically verify each op's output.
misconceptions.whyWrong: FakeTensors have no data; no numerical comparison happens.

misconceptions.claim: FakeTensor propagation eliminates the need for meta implementations of ops.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Meta impls are exactly what enable FakeTensor propagation.

implementationFacts: Each op's meta impl determines output shape/dtype from input FakeTensors
SymInts propagate alongside FakeTensor metadata for dynamic shapes
performanceScenarios: FakeTensor propagation is what makes tracing cheap: no GPU work is done during trace.
